texts: Broad fistulas between the RV and the coronary arteries can be directly ligated on the surface of the heart: E.
When the coronary circulation does not depend on the RV, a large fistula can be tied off where it runs on the epicardium, removing the steal into the coronary system.

Treatment otherwise follows the size of the RV: with a reasonable RV it is decompressed (valvotomy or a transannular patch), often with a shunt; a severely hypoplastic RV, or an RV-dependent coronary circulation, leads to the single-ventricle path.
Decompression can make narrow sinusoids regress, but decompressing an RV on which the coronaries depend can be fatal.
In the picture, the broad tunnel from the blue room into the crown spike is tied off on the outside wall.
Memory hook: a broad fist-tunnel to the crown is tied off on the outside.
